newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures slide, end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures slide, end sharply lower.

text.p: A late-afternoon slide shoved U.S. stock index futures to hefty daily losses Wednesday, more than wiping out Tuesday's gain.
Brokers tied the drop, which accelerated when U.S. Treasury bond futures ended weak, to technical selling that appeared on rallies after futures failed to keep early gains.
June Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures slid below support zones, hitting stops and drawing periodic arbitrage sell programs as the premium shrank toward 4.00 points.
Fair value Wednesday was roughly 5.75 points. Arbitrage sell programs required about 4.55 points over cash or less.
Buy programs would have needed at least 6.35 points over.
During the afternoon selloff, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell more than 50 points, triggering the New York Stock Exchange's curb on computer-assisted arbitrage.
Traders said the selloff, which occurred after three days of higher prices accompanied by rising open interest, likely drew power as some of the weaker longs bailed out.
They also cited one investment bank as a good seller at the open, during the fall to day's low and again on the close.
But the selloff stalled at Tuesday's low at 763.60, and the contract subsequently cut its biggest losses.
Some brokers said below 763.60, the next key support did not cross until the 751.30 area, although others pegged interim level at 757.50.
Sentiment began to shift again, with brokers now wondering whether the three-day upside correction might have ended and the downtrend resumed.
"All we saw here was a three-day technical bounce because the market was oversold," said one floor analyst. "It's just no good. The market is going to have a real tough time working on the upside."
"People will sell rallies," the analyst added. "I think we've got another $10 (down) to go here."
Cash S&P 500s briefly pierced key support near the 760 level, roughly where it ended the session.
"The 760 level was kind of a critical level before because it was an uptrend level," said Jay Hohmann, head futures trader, Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.
He also said an old trendline crosses in the low 750-area, which could provide support in the cash index.
"(At) 750 I think is still kind of a psychological level," Hohmann added.

June S&P 500s settled down 6.45 points at 765.60, Value Lines lost 2.65 to 694.45, Nikkei fell 265.0 to 17,830.0, Midcap eased 0.25 to 258.25, NYSE Composite lost 3.25 to 402.25, Russell 2000 rose 0.75 to 349.75, and Nasdaq 100 skidded 14.75 to 836.75.
